source_text: ἱερεὺς τὴν θυσίαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὴν σπονδὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ξυρήσεται ὁ ηὐγμένος παρὰ τὰς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου τὴν κεφαλὴν τῆς εὐχῆς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπιθήσει τὰς τρίχας ἐπὶ τὸ πῦρ, ὅ ἐστιν ὑπὸ τὴν θυσίαν τοῦ σωτηρίου. Καὶ λήψεται ὁ ἱερεὺς τὸν βραχίονα ἑφθὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ κριοῦ, καὶ ἄρτον ἕνα ἄζυμον ἀπὸ τοῦ κανοῦ, καὶ λάγανον ἄζυμον ἓν, καὶ ἐπιθήσει ἐπὶ τὰς χεῖρας τοῦ ηὐγμένου μετὰ τὸ ξυρήσασθαι αὐτὸν τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσοίσει αὐτὰ ὁ ἱερεὺς ἐπίθεμα ἔναντι Κυρίου. Ἅγιον ἔσται τῷ ἱερεῖ ἐπὶ τοῦ στηθηνίου τοῦ ἐπιθέματος, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ βραχίονος τοῦ ἀφαιρέματος, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα, πίεται ὁ ηὐγμένος οἶνον. Οὗτος ὁ νόμος τοῦ εὐξαμένου, ὃς ἂν εὔξηται δῶρον αὐτοῦ Κυρίῳ περὶ τῆς εὐχῆς, χωρὶς ὧν ἂν εὕρῃ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ κατὰ δύναμιν τῆς εὐχῆς αὐτοῦ, ἣν ἂν εὔξηται κατὰ νόμον ἁγνείας.» Ἀποφορτισάμενος γὰρ ὥσπερ τῆς Μωσαϊκῆς ἱστορίας τὸ πάχος, καὶ λατρείας τῆς ἐν τύπῳ καὶ σκιαῖς, οἱονεί τινος κόμης μακρᾶς καὶ διαβριθοῦς, ἀπαλλάξας τὸν νοῦν, ὁ ἐποφλήσας Θεῷ τὴν εἴς γε τὸ δεῖν ἁγνίσασθαι προσευχὴν, τρίχα δὲ ὥσπερ ἀναβλαστοῦσαν ἔχων τῶν διὰ Χριστοῦ θεσπισμάτων τὴν ἁγνοποιὸν ἀληθῶς εἴδησίν τε καὶ παίδευσιν, ἅγιος ἔσται καὶ ἱερὸς, καὶ πρός γε δὴ τούτῳ καὶ ἀξιόληπτος. Ἀνοίσειε δ' ἂν ἑαυτὸν εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ θυσίαν ὥσπερ ἀναθήσει δεκτὴν, τῆς ἑαυτοῦ πολιτείας τὴν εὐκλεᾶ καὶ ἀμώμητον ἀστειότητα. «Προσοίσει γὰρ, φησὶ, τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ, ἀμνὸν ἐνιαύσιον, εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα, καὶ ἀμνάδα πάλιν εἰς ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ μὴν καὶ κριὸν εἰς σωτήριον, καὶ κανοῦν ἀζύμων, ἐλαίῳ δεδευμένων, καὶ λάγανα ἄζυμα κεχρισμένα ἐλαίῳ.» Καὶ διὰ μὲν τοῦ ἀμνοῦ νοοῖτ' ἂν εἰκότως τοῦ τὴν θυσίαν προσάγοντος ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ νηπιότης, διὰ δέ γε τοῦ κριοῦ τὸ ἐν φρεσί τε καὶ ὡς ἐν καρποφορίᾳ τέλειον. «Ἀδελφοὶ γὰρ, φησὶ, μὴ παιδία γίνεσθε ταῖς φρεσὶν, ἀλλὰ τῇ κακίᾳ νηπιάζετε, ταῖς δὲ φρεσὶ τέλειοι γίνεσθε.» Διὰ μέσου δὲ ἀμνὰς, ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας. Δι' οὗ δὴ πάλιν ἡμῖν καταθρῆσαι ῥᾷον, ὅτι καὶ τῶν ἄγαν ἁγνιζομένων ὁ βίος, καὶ ὡς ἐν ἁπλότητι καὶ ἀκακίᾳ τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ νοουμένῃ, καὶ ἐν ἀρτιότητι νοῦ τετελειωμένων, οὐκ ἀμώμητος παντελῶς, δεῖται δὲ δὴ πάντως καθαρισμοῦ. Κεκτήσεται μὲν γὰρ τὸ ἀκατάσκεπτον παντελῶς οὐδεὶς, τετήρηται δὲ μόνῳ καὶ ὡς ἴδιον ἀνακείσεται τῷ Ἐμμανουὴλ τὸ σὺν ἀληθείᾳ φράσαι, «Ἔρχεται γὰρ ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἐν ἐμοὶ εὑρήσει οὐδέν.» Οὐκοῦν ἐν μὲν τῷ ἀμνῷ, καὶ τῇ ἀμνάδι, καὶ τῷ κριῷ, κατίδοι τις ἂν ὅπερ ἔφην· ἐν δέ γε τοῖς ἄρτοις τοῖς οὐκ ἐζυμωμένοις ὁ ἄδολός τε καὶ καθαρὸς σημαίνεται βίος. Ἐπιστέλλει γάρ που καὶ ὁ σοφώτατος Παῦλος τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις· «Ἐκκαθάρατε οὖν τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην, ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα, καθώς ἐστε ἄζυμοι.» Ἐν δέ γε τῷ λαγάνῳ τὸ ἥδυσμα καὶ οἱονεὶ τὸ γλυκὺ τῆς τῶν ἁγίων ζωῆς. Ἑαυτοὺς οὖν ἄρα προσοίσομεν, ὡς ἐν ἀμνῷ μὲν διὰ τὸ νήπιον ἐν Χριστῷ· ὡς ἐν ἀμνάδι δὲ αὖ, διὰ τὸ τῆς φύσεως ἀσθενὲς καὶ εὐπάροιστον εἰς τὸ πλημμελές· ἀσθενείας γὰρ τύπος τὸ θῆλυ· ὡς ἐν κριῷ δὲ δὴ, τέλειοι, καὶ εἰς
pass_a_gloss: Cyril (the quotation continues): '[the] priest [shall make] his sacrifice and his libation (σπονδή); and the one who has vowed (ὁ ηὐγμένος) shall shave beside the doors of the tent of witness the head of his vow, and shall put the hairs upon the fire, which is under the sacrifice of salvation. And the priest shall take the boiled arm (βραχίων) from the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall put [them] upon the hands of the one who has vowed after he has shaved his head, and the priest shall bring them as a placed-on offering (ἐπίθεμα) before the Lord. It shall be holy to the priest upon the breast of the placed-on offering, and upon the arm of the portion taken off (ἀφαίρεμα); and after these things the one who has vowed shall drink wine. This is the law of the one who vowed, whoever vows his gift to the Lord concerning the vow, apart from what his hand may find, according to the power of his vow, which he vows according to the law of purity (ἁγνεία).' For having unloaded as it were (ἀποφορτισάμενος) the thickness (πάχος) of the Mosaic history, and having freed the mind from the worship in type and shadows as from some long and heavy head of hair, the one who has come to owe (ἐποφλήσας) to God the prayer to be purified, and having as it were sprouting hair, the truly purifying (ἁγνοποιός) knowledge and training of the decrees given through Christ, will be holy and consecrated, and besides this also acceptable (ἀξιόληπτος). And he would offer himself for an odor of fragrance to God, and will dedicate as it were an accepted sacrifice, the glorious and blameless refinement (ἀστειότης) of his own way of life. 'For he shall bring,' he says, 'his gift: a year-old lamb for a whole burnt offering, and again a ewe lamb (ἀμνάς) for sin, and indeed also a ram for salvation, and a basket of unleavened [loaves] moistened with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil.' And through the lamb would fittingly be understood the infancy in Christ (νηπιότης) of the one bringing the sacrifice, and through the ram what is perfect (τέλειον) in mind and as in fruit-bearing. 'For brothers,' he says, 'do not become children in your minds (φρένες), but in wickedness be infants, and in your minds become perfect.' And in the middle a ewe lamb, for sin. Through which again it is easier for us to observe that even the life of those who are greatly purified, and as in the simplicity and innocence understood in Christ, and perfected in soundness (ἀρτιότης) of mind, is not wholly blameless, but in every way needs cleansing. For no one will possess the wholly irreproachable (ἀκατάσκεπτον), but it has been reserved for Emmanuel alone, and will be laid up as his own, to say with truth: 'For the ruler of this age is coming, and in me he will find nothing.' Therefore in the lamb, and the ewe lamb, and the ram, one might see what I said; and in the loaves not leavened the guileless and pure life is signified. For the most wise Paul also writes somewhere to the sanctified: 'Cleanse out therefore the old leaven, so that you may be a new lump, just as you are unleavened.' And in the wafer [is] the relish (ἥδυσμα) and as it were the sweetness of the life of the saints. We will offer ourselves then: as in a lamb, on account of what is infant in Christ; as in a ewe lamb in turn, on account of the weakness of nature and its being easily goaded (εὐπάροιστον) into fault; for the female [is] a type of weakness; as in a ram, perfect, and having reached into' [the phrase runs on into section 25].
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: ΚΥΡ. (quotation resumes) ‘[ὁ ἱερεὺς] τὴν θυσίαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σπονδήν; ξυρήσεται ὁ ηὐγμένος (the one vowed) at the doors of the tent of witness τὴν κεφαλὴν τῆς εὐχῆς, ἐπιθήσει τὰς τρίχας ἐπὶ τὸ πῦρ under τὴν θυσίαν τοῦ σωτηρίου; the priest λήψεται τὸν βραχίονα ἑφθόν (the boiled arm/shoulder) from the ram, ἄρτον ἕνα ἄζυμον from the basket, λάγανον ἄζυμον ἕν; ἐπιθήσει on the hands of the ηὐγμένος after he shaves; προσοίσει αὐτὰ ἐπίθεμα (as a placed-on/wave offering) before the Lord; ἅγιον ἔσται τῷ ἱερεῖ ἐπὶ τοῦ στηθυνίου τοῦ ἐπιθέματος (with the breast of the wave offering) καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ βραχίονος τοῦ ἀφαιρέματος (arm of the portion taken off/heave offering); after this πίεται ὁ ηὐγμένος οἶνον. This is the law of the one vowing, who vows δῶρον to the Lord περὶ τῆς εὐχῆς, χωρὶς ὧν ἂν εὕρῃ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ (apart from what his hand finds) κατὰ δύναμιν τῆς εὐχῆς, which he vows κατὰ νόμον ἁγνείας’. Exposition: ἀποφορτισάμενος (having unloaded) τῆς Μωσαϊκῆς ἱστορίας τὸ πάχος (thickness/grossness) and λατρεία ἐν τύπῳ καὶ σκιαῖς, as from κόμη μακρά καὶ διαβριθής (long, heavy hair), ἀπαλλάξας τὸν νοῦν; ὁ ἐποφλήσας Θεῷ (the one indebted to God) the προσευχή/vow εἰς τὸ ἁγνίσασθαι; having like ἀναβλαστοῦσαν τρίχα (sprouting hair) the ἁγνοποιόν (purifying) εἴδησις and παίδευσις of θεσπίσματα through Christ; ἅγιος, ἱερός, ἀξιόληπτος (acceptable). ἀνοίσειε ἑαυτόν (would offer himself) εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας; ἀναθήσει as θυσία δεκτή the εὐκλεᾶ καὶ ἀμώμητον ἀστειότητα (glorious, blameless refinement) τῆς πολιτείας. ‘προσοίσει τὸ δῶρον: ἀμνὸν ἐνιαύσιον εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα, ἀμνάδα πάλιν εἰς ἁμαρτίαν, κριὸν εἰς σωτήριον, κανοῦν ἀζύμων ἐλαίῳ δεδευμένων (moistened), λάγανα ἄζυμα κεχρισμένα ἐλαίῳ’. Through the ἀμνός: ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ νηπιότης (infancy in Christ) of the offerer; through the κριός: τὸ ἐν φρεσί (in mind) and ἐν καρποφορίᾳ τέλειον (mature). ‘ἀδελφοί, μὴ παιδία γίνεσθε ταῖς φρεσίν, ἀλλὰ τῇ κακίᾳ νηπιάζετε, ταῖς δὲ φρεσὶ τέλειοι γίνεσθε’. In the middle the ἀμνάς ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτίας: even of those ἄγαν ἁγνιζομένων (greatly purified), in ἁπλότης and ἀκακία ἐν Χριστῷ, τετελειωμένων ἐν ἀρτιότητι νοῦ (perfected in soundness of mind), the βίος is οὐκ ἀμώμητος παντελῶς, δεῖται καθαρισμοῦ. No one κεκτήσεται τὸ ἀκατάσκεπτον παντελῶς (wholly beyond scrutiny); τετήρηται (reserved) to Emmanuel alone, ὡς ἴδιον ἀνακείσεται, to say σὺν ἀληθείᾳ: ‘ἔρχεται ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, καὶ ἐν ἐμοὶ εὑρήσει οὐδέν’. In the lamb, ewe lamb and ram see what I said; in ἄρτοις οὐκ ἐζυμωμένοις ὁ ἄδολος καὶ καθαρὸς βίος; Paul ἐπιστέλλει to the ἡγιασμένοι: ‘ἐκκαθάρατε τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην, ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα, καθώς ἐστε ἄζυμοι’. In the λάγανον τὸ ἥδυσμα (relish), τὸ γλυκύ of the saints’ life. So we will offer ourselves: as in a lamb, διὰ τὸ νήπιον ἐν Χριστῷ; as in a ewe lamb, διὰ τὸ τῆς φύσεως ἀσθενές καὶ εὐπάροιστον εἰς τὸ πλημμελές (easily goaded to fault); ἀσθενείας τύπος τὸ θῆλυ; as in a ram, τέλειοι καὶ εἰς [μέτρον ἡλικίας ἐλάσαντες] (column breaks).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …offer his sacrifice and his drink offering. And the one who has vowed shall shave the head of his vow at the doors of the tent of witness, and lay the hair on the fire that is under the sacrifice of the peace offering. And the priest shall take the boiled arm of the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall put them on the hands of the one who has vowed, after he has shaved his head; and the priest shall bring them as a wave offering before the Lord. It shall be holy to the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering and the arm of the heave offering; and after this the one who has vowed shall drink wine. This is the law of the one who vows, whoever vows his gift to the Lord for his vow, besides whatever his hand can find, according to the measure of the vow he vows, according to the law of purity’ (Numbers 6:17–21). For when the one who owes God the vow to purify himself has, as it were, thrown off the burden of the coarseness of the Mosaic history, and has freed his mind from worship in type and shadows as from a long and heavy head of hair, and has instead, like hair growing again, the truly purifying knowledge and teaching of the decrees given through Christ, he will be holy and consecrated, and acceptable besides. He would offer himself to God as a fragrant aroma, and will dedicate to him, as it were an acceptable sacrifice, the glorious and blameless excellence of his own way of life. ‘For he shall bring,’ it says, ‘his gift: a lamb a year old for a whole burnt offering, and again a ewe lamb for a sin offering, and also a ram for a peace offering, and a basket of unleavened loaves moistened with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil’ (Numbers 6:14–15). By the lamb we may fitly understand the childlikeness in Christ of the one who brings the sacrifice, and by the ram what is mature in mind and, as it were, in bearing fruit. For he says: ‘Brothers, do not be children in your minds; rather, be infants in evil, but in your minds be mature’ (1 Corinthians 14:20). Between them stands the ewe lamb, offered for sin. Through this again it is easier for us to see that even the life of those who are thoroughly purified, who live, as it were, in the simplicity and innocence understood in Christ and have been made perfect in soundness of mind, is not wholly without blame, but certainly needs cleansing. For no one will possess what is wholly beyond reproach. It is reserved for Emmanuel alone, and will remain his own, to say in truth: ‘For the ruler of this age is coming, and he will find nothing in me’ (John 14:30). So in the lamb, the ewe lamb and the ram one may see what I have said. In the unleavened loaves the sincere and pure life is signified; for the most wise Paul writes somewhere to the sanctified: ‘So clean out the old leaven, so that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened’ (1 Corinthians 5:7). And in the wafer is the savor, and as it were the sweetness, of the life of the saints. We shall offer ourselves, then: as in a lamb, because of our infancy in Christ; as in a ewe lamb, because of the weakness of our nature and how easily it is driven to wrongdoing, for the female is a type of weakness; as in a ram, mature and having reached…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 16. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.
ἀκατάσκεπτον may be a corruption of ἀκατάψεκτον; either gives 'wholly beyond reproach'.

The whole section is one Cyril turn continuing from §23. Numbers 6:17–21 follows Cyril’s LXX text: βραχίων rendered ‘arm’ (English Bibles: ‘shoulder’) because Cyril reads it in §26 as a type of strength; §26 keeps ‘arm’. ἐπίθεμα rendered ‘wave offering’ and ἀφαίρεμα ‘heave offering’, following the Hebrew sense of the verse; στηθύνιον ‘breast’. ἐπὶ τοῦ στηθυνίου rendered ‘together with the breast’. ‘Fragrant aroma’ (εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας) is standard sacrificial language (Leviticus 1:9; Ephesians 5:2); no single source, so uncited. The second Numbers quotation (6:14–15) is Cyril’s loose recall with his own connectives (‘again’, ‘also’). ‘Childlikeness in Christ’ (ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ νηπιότης) may echo 1 Corinthians 3:1 (νήπιοι ἐν Χριστῷ) but Cyril uses it in a good sense; uncited. John 14:30: Cyril reads ‘ruler of this age … will find nothing in me’ (NT: τοῦ κόσμου ἄρχων … οὐκ ἔχει οὐδέν); translated as Cyril gives it. ἀκατάσκεπτον (‘beyond scrutiny’) is an odd word here and may be a corruption of ἀκατάψεκτον (‘blameless’); the sense ‘wholly beyond reproach’ fits either. εὐπάροιστον rendered ‘how easily it is driven to’. The section breaks mid-sentence (εἰς | μέτρον ἡλικίας).
